'''Operations''' are multi-stage, instanced scenarios introduced to the Live game in update 4.4.0.0 on 30 June 2026. They combine ship and on-foot objectives, squad formation, matchmaking, an Operation Runner deployment vessel, selectable difficulty, and a dedicated reward system.<ref name="operations4400">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/updates/4-4-0-0 Elite Dangerous: Operations – Available Now], Frontier Developments, 30 June 2026.</ref>

Operations are not ordinary [[Missions|Mission Board missions]]. They also should not be confused with older references to an Odyssey Mission Board '''Operations''' category or the generic use of ''operation'' for a multi-step activity.

Frontier launched Operations as a '''Networking & Balancing Beta''' so it could monitor connectivity and server load in the live environment while making performance and balance adjustments more frequently. Frontier continued to use that framing when update 4.4.2.0 and Found Adrift were released.<ref name="operations4400" /><ref name="anacondaupdateforum">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/elite-dangerous-anaconda-mk-ii-update.650380/ Elite Dangerous: Anaconda Mk II Update], Frontier Developments, 20 October 2026.</ref>

== Starting an Operation ==

# Dock at an eligible market location.
# Open the Operations interface from the ship panel.
# Select a scenario, difficulty, and mode.
# Form a squad or use optional matchmaking.
# Select the ship required for the run before launch.
# Ready up and deploy aboard the Operation Runner.

A commander can start alone, but Frontier describes Operations as team-focused and recommends strong equipment for solo attempts. NPCs do not fill squad positions; a squad contains up to four players.<ref name="junelog">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/elite-dangerous-june-dev-log-2026 Elite Dangerous: June Dev Log 2026], Frontier Developments, 19 June 2026.</ref>

Ships cannot be changed after an Operation begins. Suits can be changed by returning to the commander's ship during a suitable stage.<ref name="junelog" />

== Operation Runner and redeployment ==

The '''Operation Runner''' carries the squad to the scenario and acts as its central deployment point. Operations use bespoke isolated instances selected for the scenario.

When defeated:

* ship stages return the commander to the Operation Runner or the last operation-specific dock;
* on-foot stages return the commander to the ship for redeployment;
* redeploying during the Operation has no ordinary death penalty under the feature's rules.<ref name="operations4400" />

Before entry, the game temporarily stores the commander's existing bounties, fines, and bonds to prevent repeated deaths or scenario failure from applying unintended losses.<ref name="operations4400" />

== Modes ==

=== Mercenary Mode ===

Mercenary Mode is the standard form. It has no Powerplay effect and is available to commanders who meet the selected scenario's requirements.

=== Powerplay Mode ===

Powerplay Mode allows an eligible squad to undermine a selected Power. The squad cannot target a Power represented by one of its members. Unaligned commanders can participate but do not earn Merits.<ref name="operations4400" />

Powerplay eligibility and the target Power should be checked before launch; ordinary Operation rewards and Powerplay consequences are separate decisions.

== Scenarios ==

Eight Operations are available through update 4.4.2.0. Six launched with update 4.4.0.0:<ref name="operations4400" />

* '''Terminal Prosecution''' — clear a criminal force through combat stages.
* '''Tactical Takedown''' — board a compromised megaship, obtain intelligence, and pursue the responsible commander.
* '''Firestorm Rescue''' — break a siege and evacuate hostages from a burning station while managing heat and attackers.
* '''Rapid Response''' — evacuate a planetary port before a larger hostile fleet arrives.
* '''Reclamation Point''' — clear hostile forces in and around a hijacked megaship.
* '''Biohazard Takedown''' — assault a research operation, identify responsible researchers, and eliminate the threat.

'''Under Siege''' was added for all players on 2 September 2026. It responds to a planetary-settlement distress call, combining ship combat to break a blockade with on-foot combat to retake the facility and a later ship threat.<ref name="auglog">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/elite-dangerous-august-dev-log-2026 Elite Dangerous: August Dev Log 2026], Frontier Developments, 27 August 2026.</ref>

'''Found Adrift''' was added on 20 October 2026 with update 4.4.2.0. Commanders investigate a long-missing megaship that has reappeared without communications, enter its damaged interior, locate a vault, recover a high-value asset, and fight rival scavengers during the extraction.<ref name="octlog">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/elite-dangerous-october-dev-log-2026-law-disorder Elite Dangerous: October Dev Log 2026 | Law & Disorder], Frontier Developments, 14 October 2026.</ref><ref name="update4420">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/updates/4-4-2-0 Elite Dangerous: Anaconda Mk II Update 4.4.2.0], Frontier Developments, 20 October 2026.</ref>

Update 4.4.2.0 also improved the cutting tool's tracking.<ref name="update4420" />

Scenario names and individual stage details should be taken from the current interface because Operations is still receiving new content and balance updates.

== Difficulty and preparation ==

Easy and Hard use the same broad scenario concept but differ in opposition and reward value. Frontier's launch recommendations range from A-rated ships with little or no Engineering for some Easy scenarios to fully engineered ships and Grade 4–5 on-foot equipment for Hard variants.<ref name="operations4400" />

Before launch, agree on:

* ship roles and engineering;
* suit and weapon loadouts;
* rescue or evacuation capacity where required;
* who handles scanning, boarding, or objective interactions;
* target priorities and regroup points;
* whether the run uses Mercenary or Powerplay Mode.

The recommended player count varies by scenario, commonly two to four or three to four. A solo run is possible but is a challenge choice rather than the baseline design.<ref name="junelog" />

== Rewards ==

Completing an Operation can award:

* credits;
* materials;
* '''Merc Coins''';
* Merits from eligible Powerplay Mode runs.

Hard difficulty provides greater reward value, while the selected Operation is the main factor determining the reward pool.<ref name="junelog" />

Merc Coins are not redeemed at one dedicated Merc Store. They are spent through existing vendors at relevant locations. Launch rewards include base-level ship modules through Outfitting and blueprints through Engineers; eligible equipment can then be upgraded through the appropriate Engineer.<ref name="operations4400" />

See [[Merc Coin]] for the current acquisition and vendor details.

== Failure and restart behaviour ==

Operations are staged activities rather than contracts that end at the first death. Redeployment returns the commander to the scenario as described above. A stage can still fail through its own objective, timer, or scenario conditions, and the squad should follow the current objective panel rather than assuming unlimited recovery makes every state reversible.

Update 4.4.0.3 corrected reward-screen and objective-tracking problems, while 4.4.1.0 and 4.4.1.1 continued Operations fixes. Update 4.4.2.0 fixed the missing final on-foot enemy wave in Reclamation Point. These updates reinforce that older launch-day reports may not describe current behaviour.<ref name="update4403">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/update-notes/4-4-0-3 Elite Dangerous 4.4.0.3 Update Notes], Frontier Developments, 9 July 2026.</ref><ref name="update4420" />

== Relationship to missions and BGS ==

Operations use their own access, deployment, modes, objectives, and rewards. They should not be placed under a normal mission-type page merely because each scenario contains mission-like stages.

Mercenary Mode has no Powerplay consequences according to Frontier. Powerplay Mode has explicit undermining and Merit rules. Frontier's published Operations material does not establish ordinary minor-faction influence effects equivalent to Mission Board INF rewards; do not claim such BGS effects without current journal or in-game evidence.
